question: What is MPP on Stellar, what payment modes does it support, and how should an API advertise that agents can pay it?

golden.answer: MPP is an HTTP-402 payment protocol. On Stellar, Charge settles a SAC transfer per request on-chain, and Session uses a funded channel with cumulative off-chain commitments. An API advertises payment through an OpenAPI 3.1 document with x-payment-info.offers, but the runtime 402 challenge is authoritative for price, token, network and expiry. MPP and x402 both use HTTP 402 with different payloads and headers; never relabel one as the other.
keyFacts: MPP Charge settles a SAC transfer per request; Session uses a funded off-chain channel.
APIs advertise MPP via OpenAPI x-payment-info; the runtime 402 challenge is authoritative.
x402 and MPP both use HTTP 402 but are distinct protocols with distinct payloads.
avoid: Do NOT claim MPP Session needs a new on-chain transfer for every call.
Do NOT claim an MPP directory listing verifies client payments, or relabel one protocol's payload as the other's.
golden.notes: A single mppx endpoint serving both protocols, or separate adapters, is acceptable (mpp.dev, as of 2026-11-14).

sources.note: Run x402 inline with mppx: one route returns MPP and x402 Challenges, accepts either Credential, returns the matching Receipt
Negotiator selects MPP or x402 per request and rejects a request that carries both credentials

corroboration.claim: MPP uses HTTP 402; Stellar Charge settles SAC transfers per request and Session uses cumulative off-chain channel commitments.

evidence.note: 'It extends the `402 Payment Required` HTTP status code into a machine-readable payment negotiation layer' and Charge: 'Each request triggers a Soroban SAC `transfer` settled on-chain individually.' Session: 'The funder deposits tokens into the channel once, then makes many off-chain payments by signing cumulative commitments'.
'Each commitment is cumulative. The server tracks the highest commitment it has seen; closing the channel batch-settles all payments in a single on-chain transaction.'
'**charge** for one-time on-chain transfers'; the second intent is still labeled 'channel' here, while SDF docs say 'session'.
'Session mode (channel-backed off-chain commits, high-frequency; formerly called Channel mode)'.

corroboration.claim: Publish OpenAPI 3.1, commonly at /openapi.json, with x-payment-info.offers.

evidence.note: 'You serve a standard OpenAPI 3.1 document at `/openapi.json` with `x-payment-info` extensions' and 'canonical `x-payment-info.offers[]` entries on each paid route'.
'A paid MPP server publishes an OpenAPI 3.1 document at `GET /openapi.json`. Each paid operation carries an `x-payment-info` extension holding an `offers[]` array.'

corroboration.claim: Discovery metadata is advisory; the runtime 402 Challenge controls current price, token, network, expiry, and terms.

evidence.note: 'Discovery documents are informational hints. The runtime `402` Challenge remains the authoritative source of payment terms.'
'The runtime **402 Challenge is authoritative** for price, token, network, expiry, and terms.'

corroboration.claim: MPPScan and the mpp.dev services registry, including https://mpp.dev/mcp/services, are optional discovery surfaces.

evidence.note: Lists '[MPPScan](https://mppscan.com) | Public registry of MPP-enabled services' and 'Agents can query the curated services directory over MCP at `https://mpp.dev/mcp/services`. The server is read-only'.
MCP initialize returned HTTP 200 with serverInfo name 'mpp-services-mcp', version 1.0.0.
'Agents can query the curated directory over MCP at `https://mpp.dev/mcp/services`. That server is read-only.'

corroboration.claim: MPP and x402 are distinct protocols; one mppx endpoint can serve both, but payloads must not be relabeled.

evidence.note: Challenge header is 'PAYMENT-REQUIRED' for x402 and 'WWW-Authenticate: Payment' for MPP. 'You can run both protocols on the same endpoint with mppx'.
mppx can serve both protocols on one endpoint, but 'The wrapper delegates x402 Credentials, lifecycle hooks, verification, and settlement to the official x402 adapter.'
Compares x402, MPP Charge, and MPP Session as separate columns.
'Send either an MPP credential or an x402 payment signature, not both.' (status 400)

corroboration.claim: MPP Session requires a new on-chain transfer for every API call.

evidence.note: 'no per-payment on-chain transactions, ideal for AI agent interactions'.
'No on-chain transaction is needed per payment, making this ideal for high-frequency AI agent interactions.'

corroboration.claim: Listing an API in an MPP directory automatically verifies all client payments.

evidence.note: 'The MCP server is advisory and read-only. After discovery, clients call the target service directly and treat the runtime `402` Challenge as authoritative.'
'the discovery document is advisory. Take price, token, network, expiry, and terms from the 402 Challenge.'
'Use this read-only MCP server to discover MPP paid API services'.

corroboration.claim: MPP Charge settles a Soroban SAC transfer per request on-chain.

evidence.note: Each request triggers a Soroban SAC `transfer` settled on-chain individually.

corroboration.claim: mpp.dev says one mppx endpoint can serve both MPP and x402 clients.

evidence.note: You can run both protocols on the same endpoint with `mppx`

evidence: Live A 2026-11-14: https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/agentic-payments/mpp -- 'Each request triggers a Soroban SAC `transfer` settled on-chain individually.'
Live A 2026-11-14: https://mpp.dev/mpp-vs-x402 -- 'You can run both protocols on the same endpoint with `mppx`'

truth.notes:
Status-sensitive details are stated as of 2026-11-02; grade later sourced changes leniently and require dated primary evidence.
As of 2026-11-02, https://mpp.dev/mpp-vs-x402 says one mppx endpoint can serve both protocols for x402-compatible EVM charges. An answer that recommends separate adapters, or one endpoint that offers both protocols, is not wrong. An answer that relabels one protocol's payload or headers as the other is wrong.
